title: Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
12.     MOS 2181, Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief supervise the maintenance,
repair, and inspection of all small arms weapons and towed artillery
howitzers and direct the activities of assigned enlisted personnel in a small
arms or towed artillery repair shop or facility. They supervise and manage
the administration of small arms or towed artillery maintenance facilities
and offices. The Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief is proficient in the
organization, management, operation and conduct of technical inspections of
small arms weapons, and towed artillery howitzers, all equipment, and
maintenance shops or facilities for maintaining small arms or towed artillery
howitzers. The Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief assists the Weapons Repair
Officer in all duties and tasks. They manage command environmental and
hazardous waste programs. They supervise and provide oversight of disposal,
storage, emergency planning for hazardous waste, and ozone depleting
substances. 2181 Marines possess a comprehensive knowledge of environmental
and hazardous waste programs, disposal, storage, emergency planning for
hazardous waste, and ozone depleting substances. 2181 Marines possess a
comprehensive understanding of maintenance procedures for small arms weapons,
and towed artillery howitzers, repair shop management and operations,
maintenance and supply procedures.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Hold PMOSs 2111, 2131, 2161, or 2171.

            (2) Achieve promotion to master sergeant.

    c. Requirements. It is highly recommended that the Marine complete the
Ground Ordnance Managers Course (A14GBS6) before promotion to MSgt. However,
non-completion of the course is not a disqualifier from achieving the MOS.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (au), Ground Ordnance Maintenance Training and Readiness.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-
1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Ordnance Vehicle Maintenance Chief, 2149.




                                         3-150                        Enclosure (1)
 3121                                                                      NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: The Ground Ordnance Maintenance OccFld maintains the serviceability of ground ordnance materials. Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units. Qualifications required include basic ordnance administration and knowledge; the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures. Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment. Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods. Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer. Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 2100, Basic Ground Ordnance Maintenance Marine. Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.

matches: Design and oversee testing, installation, and repair of marine apparatus and equipment.
Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units.
Examine objects, systems, or facilities and analyze information to determine needed installations, services, or repairs.
the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.

Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment.
Inspect grounds, facilities, and equipment routinely to determine necessity of repairs or maintenance.

Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods.
Troubleshoot, maintain, and make minor repairs to equipment.

Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer.
Design and oversee testing, installation, and repair of marine apparatus and equipment.
Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems.
Plan, organize, and execute logistics support activities, such as maintenance planning, repair analysis, and test equipment recommendations.

Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.
Troubleshoot, maintain, and make minor repairs to equipment.

Ground Ordnance Weapons Chief supervise the maintenance, repair, and inspection of all small arms weapons and towed artillery howitzers and direct the activities of assigned enlisted personnel in a small arms or towed artillery repair shop or facility.
Perform administrative duties, such as overseeing building management, ordering supplies, contracting for services or repairs, or supervising the work of staff members or volunteers.
They supervise and manage the administration of small arms or towed artillery maintenance facilities and offices.
Implement or oversee environmental management or sustainability programs addressing issues such as recycling, conservation, or waste management.
They manage command environmental and hazardous waste programs.
Serve as liaison with federal, state, or local agencies or officials on issues pertaining to solid or hazardous waste program requirements.
They supervise and provide oversight of disposal, storage, emergency planning for hazardous waste, and ozone depleting substances.
Develop equipment maintenance schedules and arrange for repairs.

2181 Marines possess a comprehensive understanding of maintenance procedures for small arms weapons, and towed artillery howitzers, repair shop management and operations, maintenance and supply procedures.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (au), Ground Ordnance Maintenance Training and Readiness.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
